From personal kindness to an institution
Walking to where the need is
A family that decided to serve
We don't claim to meet every need, but we respond to the ones within our reach.
entries.text: Home / About Our story It is a story about people. What started with a teacher listening to his students grew into an organization serving teachers, children, women and communities across Liberia. The beginning Founding TIME Inc. Reaching rural Liberia Training teachers Mission & values The people behind TIME It began with listening As a classroom teacher, Dr. Philip V. Saywrayne, III began noticing things that concerned him deeply. Many students, particularly young women, struggled to keep up. Some submitted assignments late or not at all. Some slept during lectures. Some young men left campus before the school day had ended. These behaviors could easily have been read as a lack of seriousness. He believed there was more to the story. He began listening and later administered a diagnostic assessment to understand what was really happening. The answers were painful but important. Students were struggling to pay school fees, buy basic materials and meet daily needs. Some worked long, difficult hours just to remain in school. Some young women had become vulnerable to exploitative survival practices because of economic hardship; some young men were exposed to theft, substances and other risks. Sometimes a student does not need another reprimand. Sometimes the student needs someone to listen, someone to care, and someone to help create a pathway through the difficulty. He and his wife began helping wherever they could. There was no organization, large budget or elaborate structure. They saw needs and responded with whatever they had: school supplies, encouragement and practical support, offered quietly and personally. From personal kindness to an institution As they heard more stories from young people, women, families and communities, it became clear that the need was far greater than two individuals could meet. The need also extended beyond the capital. Rural towns and villages had children without basic materials, teachers without professional support, and women and widows in need. That raised a simple question: if the needs are so great, and we are already trying to help, should there not be an organization through which this work can be organized, strengthened and continued? In January 2021 , the Technical Institute for Many Empowerment (TIME Inc.) was established and registered with the Government of Liberia. Dr. Saywrayne, his partner Ms. Tibeh E. Gbassagee-Saywrayne, and their daughter Ms. Tijue N. Suah developed the organization together and coined its name, a name for an institution that would not merely respond to immediate needs, but also empower people through education, professional development, skills training, humanitarian assistance and self-reliance. Our guiding Scripture “Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act.” Proverbs 3:27 (NIV). We may not be able to solve every problem, but we can do something. entries.text: Home / FAQ Questions & answers Frequently asked questions Answers about our programs, registration, online learning, Phìtìa Academy and how to support our work. Search the questions No question matches your search. Ask us directly or message us on WhatsApp . Admissions & programs Is TIME Inc. accredited? Yes. TIME Inc. is an accredited supplementary teacher-training institution under the Bureau of Teacher Education, Ministry of Education (MoE), Liberia. It was established and registered with the Government of Liberia in January 2021. What programs do you offer? We offer the "C" Certificate in Elementary Education, "C" Certificate lab training for Senior High science teachers, other skills courses such as English and research skills, 11 professional certificate programs and 10 diploma programs. See the full list on the Programs page . How long are the courses? The "C" Certificate in Elementary Education runs for nine months. Professional certificate and diploma courses run for 10 weeks each. The laboratory training for Senior High science teachers is 10 weeks plus a two-month supervised internship. Skills course durations are confirmed for each course. See all programs and fees . When are classes held? Depending on the program, enrolment and instructors, classes run on weekday afternoons, on Saturdays, or both. Typical times are: Weekday track: Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM Saturday track: Saturday only, 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM The administration gives registered students their exact timetable before classes begin. How do I register? Registration is ongoing. Visit our campus Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM, call an admissions line ( +231 880 902 568 , +231 776 037 641 , +231 777 714 784 or +231 778 138 548 ), message us on WhatsApp , or send us a message . How much do the courses cost? Approved tuition fees are: "C" Certificate in Elementary Education: US$80 (LRD 13,600) Professional certificate courses: US$125 per course Diploma courses: US$175 per course Skills courses (Standard English, Research Skills, Records Keeping): US$125 per course Laboratory training for Senior High science teachers: confirmed by the administration before registration Liberian dollar amounts use the approved rate of US$1 = LRD 170. Full fee details . Can I pay in installments? Yes, for the "C" Certificate in Elementary Education: two equal installments of US$40 (LRD 6,800), the first when you register and the second before the exit examination. For other courses, admissions will give you the approved payment schedule. All tuition must be paid before the exit examination. When does the next class start? For the 2027 intake, the registration deadline is Monday, January 4, 2027 and classes begin on Monday, March 8, 2027 . The following intake is on Thursday, October 14, 2027 . entries.text: Home / Our Founder Executive Director Dr. Philip V. Saywrayne, III An award-winning author, educator, researcher, academic administrator, consultant and project management specialist. About Dr. Saywrayne A lifelong commitment to quality education Throughout his career, Dr. Saywrayne has worked to advance quality education, strengthen educational leadership and empower underserved communities through capacity-building. As Executive Director of TIME Inc., he leads teacher education, vocational and technical training, and outreach to underprivileged women, children and other vulnerable people in Bong, Grand Bassa and Margibi Counties. He has taught undergraduate and graduate students in Research Methodology, Education, English, Sociology and Educational Leadership at the University of Liberia, Carver Christian University, Cuttington University and Trinity University Graduate School, and has mentored many students, emerging scholars and school leaders. 12 books authored Education Academic background In progress Ph.D. in Development Studies: Educational Policy & Planning Africa Research University (ARU), Lusaka, Zambia Doctorate, with distinction Ph.D. in Christian School Administration Louisiana Baptist University and Theological Seminary, Shreveport, Louisiana, USA Master's M.Ed. in Educational Administration & Supervision Cuttington University School of Graduate and Professional Studies, Liberia Bachelor's B.A. in English African Methodist Episcopal University (AMEU), Monrovia, Liberia Leadership Roles & service Current Executive Director, TIME Inc. Teacher education, technical training and community empowerment. Current Chairman, School of Education Cuttington University School of Graduate and Professional Studies. Previously Vice President for Academic Affairs Carver Christian University: academic planning, curriculum, quality assurance, accreditation and faculty development. Project management GPE Basic Education School Grants Project & Liberia's School Leadership Project Strengthened school leadership, governance and service delivery nationwide. Consulting Consulting Partner, ADARA Management and Consultancy Education policy, strategic planning and institutional strengthening. Public service Transcription Specialist, National Independent Commission of Inquiry Documented the Commission's proceedings on violence after the November 2011 run-off election. Author Selected books Dr. Saywrayne has authored 12 books on educational leadership, personal development and family life, along with peer-reviewed journal articles. Proceeds from book sales have helped fund TIME Inc.'s outreach. M Mastering School Leadership A practical guide for school leaders. Amazon publication pending. entries.text: Home / Our Impact Our work Areas where we're making a positive impact From village classrooms to graduation day, here is what your support makes possible. Focus areas What we work on 01 Preventing Educational Poverty Improving learning environments by equipping schools with textbooks, copybooks, chalkboards, benches and other essentials. 02 Teacher Professional Development Accredited training that gives teachers the pedagogy, ethics and classroom skills their learners deserve. 03 Girls' Education & Women's Empowerment Creating opportunities for girls, women and widows, offering practical support and helping protect young women from exploitation. 04 Child Protection & Health Raising awareness of child protection and safeguarding, and supporting community health campaigns that protect vulnerable children. 05 Orphans & Vulnerable Children Care, schooling and belonging for orphans and children from struggling households, including through Phìtìa Academy. 06 Climate & Child Rights Addressing environmental threats to children's well-being, supported by training in environmental health and GIS mapping. Success stories Inspiring stories from the communities we've helped 523 Children · 6 schools Grand Bassa County Reaching 523 underserved children across six remote schools We identified and connected with 523 underserved children scattered across six remote schools in Grand Bassa County. These young learners, once overlooked, are now at the center of our commitment to quality education, empowering their futures and breaking the chains of educational poverty. 122 Students supported Kpehpue Town, Grand Bassa Equipping 122 eager students at Kpehpue Town Community School Learners who had faced real barriers to education now have the tools and resources they need to thrive. Through our programs we have offered them not only the gift of knowledge but a renewed sense of hope. 2026 Graduating class Margibi campus A new class of trained professionals The TIME Inc. Class of 2026 walked across the stage in caps, gowns and green-and-red stoles. They are teachers and professionals now better equipped to serve their schools, churches and communities. What the video shows: the TIME Inc. team in white shirts driving a four-wheel-drive vehicle through flooded dirt roads, meeting parents and community members under a shelter, and standing with groups of schoolchildren in their villages. The Technical Institute for Many Empowerment (TIME) Inc. began when a teacher stopped to ask why his students were falling behind and listened to the answers. Behind the missed assignments and empty seats were stories of poverty, survival and a deep desire to stay in school. Dr. Philip V. Saywrayne, III and his wife, Mrs. Tibeh E. Gbassagee-Saywrayne, began helping quietly from their own limited resources. In January 2021 that personal commitment became TIME Inc.: a registered Liberian institution for teacher education, skills training and humanitarian service. Today we are an accredited supplementary teacher-training institution under the Bureau of Teacher Education, Ministry of Education, and we still go on foot when that's what it takes to reach a village school. entries.title: Phìtìa Academy (PHICA)
entries.description: Phìtìa Academy (PHICA) is a government-registered elementary and junior high school in Tower Hill, Margibi County, Liberia, serving vulnerable children affected by the Ebola crisis.
headings: Where others saw an empty field, the founders saw classrooms.
Children the Ebola crisis left behind
Built on sacrifice, sustained by community
More than lessons: growing whole children
Every child deserves an opportunity to learn, regardless of family circumstances or economic status.
entries.text: Home / Phìtìa Academy Est. 2023 · Sister school Phìtìa Academy (PHICA) “We shape the mind that will shape the future.” PHICA was founded to support children whose lives were disrupted by the Ebola crisis. Location Slagbaawein, Tower Hill, Lower Margibi County Education district Marshall Education District Level Nursery, Elementary & Junior High Status Registered with the Government of Liberia Our beginning Where others saw an empty field, the founders saw classrooms. Dr. Philip V. Saywrayne, III and Mrs. Tibeh E. Gbassagee-Saywrayne personally bought the land, an undeveloped field of savanna grass, and began building a school. They imagined a place where children could sit in classrooms, hold books, learn to read and write, discover their abilities and begin to imagine a different future. That vision became Phìtìa Academy. PHICA is more than a school building. It is a response to a need, an expression of hope, and a commitment to children whose circumstances should never determine the limits of their future. Meet our principal Ms. Tibeh E. Gbassagee Principal, Phìtìa Academy (PHICA) A co-founder of TIME Inc. and Phìtìa Academy, Ms. Gbassagee serves as the school principal. She has helped support students and teachers from the very beginning. Contact the school The context Children the Ebola crisis left behind During and after the Ebola crisis, many children's education was interrupted for long periods. Some lost one or both parents and were raised by relatives, neighbors or the wider community. Others grew up in families already struggling with poverty. Before PHICA, a community school was doing its best, but it lacked trained, qualified teachers and resources. At one point, three shipping containers were being used as classrooms , including for children orphaned by Ebola. A shipping container can provide temporary shelter, but it cannot by itself provide the kind of educational environment every child deserves. How PHICA works Built on sacrifice, sustained by community Founded on personal sacrifice With no major donor or grant, the founders gave portions of their own salaries to pay teachers and keep the doors open. Tuition-free for many A substantial number of pupils attend tuition-free or receive significant financial help. Poverty should never be a permanent sentence on a child's future. Community-supported Families who can contribute pay US$60 or less (Nursery – Grade 6). Contributions from families who can afford them help keep education accessible to those who cannot. Our mission More than lessons: growing whole children We want our pupils to grow academically, socially, morally and personally: to value health, hygiene, responsibility, cooperation, respect, integrity, compassion and service. A school close to home reduces the need for young children to make long, costly or unsafe journeys to learn. Improving access to elementary education Strengthening foundational literacy and numeracy Supporting children from vulnerable households Promot

entries.title: Privacy Policy
entries.description: How TIME Inc. collects, uses and protects information from website visitors, contact form messages and TIME Learning accounts.
entries.text: Home / Privacy Your information Privacy policy How TIME Inc. handles the information you share through this website, our contact form and TIME Learning. In short The public website uses no cookies, no advertising and no tracking or analytics tools . We only receive personal information that you choose to send us: through the contact form, by WhatsApp, phone or email, or by creating a TIME Learning account. We use it to answer you, to run our courses and to keep records of your learning. We do not sell it or share it for marketing. You can ask us to see, correct or delete your information at any time. Visiting the website The website is hosted by GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc.). Like any web host, GitHub automatically receives technical information such as your IP address and browser type when you load a page, and may keep it in security logs. We cannot see these logs and do not use them. Fonts and images are served from the website itself, so loading a page does not contact Google or other third parties. Links to WhatsApp, Google Maps and other sites only connect you to those services when you choose to follow them; their own privacy policies then apply. The TIME Assistant chat answers from information published on this website. What you type in it stays in your browser (kept only until you close the tab) and is not sent to us or anyone else, unless you tap a WhatsApp or contact link to ask us directly. The contact form When you send a message through our contact form , we receive your name, email address, phone or WhatsApp number (if you give it), the topic you choose and your message . The form is delivered by FormSubmit (formsubmit.co), a form-forwarding service, to the TIME Inc. office inbox at tinstitute312@gmail.com, which is a Google Gmail account. We use your details only to reply to you and to follow up on your request, such as a course registration, donation or partnership. If the form cannot send, the website offers to open your own email app or WhatsApp with your message instead. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it there. WhatsApp, phone and email If you contact us by WhatsApp, phone or email, we receive your number or email address and whatever you tell us. WhatsApp messages are handled by WhatsApp (Meta) under its own terms. We use these conversations only to respond to you and to provide the service you asked about. TIME Learning accounts If you create an account on TIME Learning , we store the information needed to run your courses: Account details: your name and email address. Passwords and sign-in are handled by Neon Auth, our account provider; we never see your password. A one-time code is emailed to you to confirm your address. Course records: course requests and approvals, your cohort, lessons you mark complete, quiz and test answers and results, written submissions and any files you upload, grades and lecturer feedback, and class attendance recorded by staff. entries.title: Is TIME Inc. accredited?
entries.description: Yes. TIME Inc. is an accredited supplementary teacher-training institution under the Bureau of Teacher Education, Ministry of Education (MoE), Liberia. It was established and registered with the Government of Liberia in January 2021.

entries.title: What programs do you offer?
entries.description: We offer the "C" Certificate in Elementary Education, "C" Certificate lab training for Senior High science teachers, other skills courses such as English and research skills, 11 professional certificate programs and 10 diploma programs. See the full list on the Programs page .

entries.title: How long are the courses?
entries.description: The "C" Certificate in Elementary Education runs for nine months. Professional certificate and diploma courses run for 10 weeks each. The laboratory training for Senior High science teachers is 10 weeks plus a two-month supervised internship. Skills course durations are confirmed for each course. Se

entries.title: When are classes held?
entries.description: Depending on the program, enrolment and instructors, classes run on weekday afternoons, on Saturdays, or both. Typical times are: Weekday track: Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM Saturday track: Saturday only, 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM The administration gives registered students their exact t

entries.title: How do I register?
entries.description: Registration is ongoing. Visit our campus Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM, call an admissions line ( +231 880 902 568 , +231 776 037 641 , +231 777 714 784 or +231 778 138 548 ), message us on WhatsApp , or send us a message .

entries.title: How much do the courses cost?
entries.description: Approved tuition fees are: "C" Certificate in Elementary Education: US$80 (LRD 13,600) Professional certificate courses: US$125 per course Diploma courses: US$175 per course Skills courses (Standard English, Research Skills, Records Keeping): US$125 per course Laboratory training for Senior High sci

entries.title: Can I pay in installments?
entries.description: Yes, for the "C" Certificate in Elementary Education: two equal installments of US$40 (LRD 6,800), the first when you register and the second before the exit examination. For other courses, admissions will give you the approved payment schedule. All tuition must be paid before the exit examination.

entries.title: When does the next class start?
entries.description: For the 2027 intake, the registration deadline is Monday, January 4, 2027 and classes begin on Monday, March 8, 2027 . The following intake is on Thursday, October 14, 2027 . These dates apply unless TIME Inc. issues an official written notice changing them.

entries.title: Are there other fees besides tuition?
entries.description: A registration/application fee of US$15 applies where applicable, in addition to tuition. The exit examination fee is US$10 (LRD 1,700) , paid before the examination date and separate from tuition. You must also have paid all tuition and received financial clearance before you sit the exit examinati

entries.title: What does the tuition fee cover?
entries.description: Unless stated in writing, tuition covers instruction only. Before you enroll, admissions will tell you whether learning materials, assessments and exams, certificate or diploma processing, internship costs or other charges are included or charged separately.

entries.title: Are discounts or scholarships available?
entries.description: TIME Inc. may grant a 50% tuition discount , subject to eligibility and approval, to eligible staff of Phìtìa Academy (PHICA), approved groups enrolling together, and students who meet the early-payment conditions. The discount applies to tuition only, not registration, exam, materials or certificat

entries.title: How do I pay, and when do I get my certificate?
entries.description: Before you enroll, admissions will tell you every fee and charge and give you the approved payment schedule for your program. Pay only through official TIME Inc. payment channels, such as Mobile Money to 0888 901 848 (Lonestar Cell MTN, name: Philip V. Saywrayne), and keep every official receipt as

entries.title: Where are classes held?
entries.description: At the Phìtìa Academy (PHICA) campus, Slagbaawein Oldfield, Live Smart Community, Tower Hill, behind Christian Aid Ministries, Robertsfield Highway, Margibi County. Get directions .

entries.title: Who teaches the courses?
entries.description: Our lecturers hold qualifications ranging from master’s to PhD degrees.

entries.title: Can I study online?
entries.description: Yes, for the Special Education Support Training Cohort #1. It is a 10-week program delivered 60% online and 40% in person, through the TIME Learning portal .

entries.title: How do I get into the learning portal?
entries.description: Create a student account, verify your email address and request enrolment in your course. Once TIME approves your enrolment, your course materials, assignments and class schedule appear in your account. Start at Online Learning .

entries.title: What is Phìtìa Academy?
entries.description: Phìtìa Academy (PHICA) is TIME Inc.’s sister school: a government-registered nursery, elementary and junior high school in Tower Hill, Margibi County, founded to support children whose lives were disrupted by the Ebola crisis. Learn more about PHICA .

entries.title: How much does PHICA cost?
entries.description: Many pupils attend tuition-free or receive significant financial help. Families who can contribute pay US$60 or less (Nursery – Grade 6).

entries.title: How do I enrol my child at PHICA?
entries.description: Visit the school, call +231 777 891 104 , or send us a message about enrollment.

entries.title: How can I donate?
entries.description: See Donate for what your gift provides and how to give from Liberia or abroad. In Liberia, you can send a gift by Mobile Money to 0888 901 848 (Lonestar Cell MTN, name: Philip V. Saywrayne). After sending, or to give from abroad, message us on WhatsApp .

entries.title: What does my donation pay for?
entries.description: Textbooks, copybooks and pencils for rural schools; benches and chalkboards; scholarships for vulnerable children at Phìtìa Academy; teacher training and salaries; and water and sanitation at PHICA.

entries.title: Can I give books or supplies instead of money?
entries.description: Yes. Textbooks, copybooks, pencils, reading books, shoes and school supplies all reach children directly. See what we need .

entries.title: Can I volunteer?
entries.description: Yes. You can join outreach trips, teach a class, mentor students, or lend professional skills in health, finance, media or education. Tell us how you would like to help .

entries.title: Can my organization partner with TIME?
entries.description: We welcome churches, schools, NGOs, businesses and development partners who want to help scale teacher training and community outreach. Get in touch .

entries.title: When is the office open?
entries.description: You can visit our campus Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM.

entries.title: What is the best way to reach you?
entries.description: Call +231 777 891 104 , WhatsApp +231 888 901 848 , email tinstitute312@gmail.com , or use our contact form .
